parole.significato: autopsy (post-mortem examination involving dissection of the body)
parole.testo: 18th century, from Ancient Greek αὐτοψία (autopsía). The specific contemporary sense (late 19th century) after French autopsie.

Early 16th century in the sense “comedic”, directly from Latin com(icus) + -isch, from Ancient Greek κωμικός (kōmikós). The broader sense “funny” since the 17th century under influence of French comique. The sense “strange” was derived thence (as in English funny).
17th century, from Ancient Greek μετεωρολογία (meteōrología), in part through French météorologie, equivalent to meteoro- + -logie.
